mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over the previous 6 months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where RSAFS increases over 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the previous 3 months signals a robust supply-side expansion, which boosts economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where INDPRO increases by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% annualized over the previous 3 months, it signals a mismatch between accommodative monetary policy and inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: accommodative monetary policy with inflationary pressure
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.5 percentage points and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over the previous 3 months, it signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decrease > 0.5pp and PAYEMS increase > 200k in 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp and PAYEMS increases by more than 200k.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over the previous 3 months signals weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where HOUST decreases by more than 10%.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and industrial production (INDPRO) decreases by more than 2% over the same period, it signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative growth for 2 quarters and INDPRO decrease > 2%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 shows negative growth for 2 quarters and INDPRO decreases by more than 2%.
